thread:
Maya P: uploading a condensed PRD for Dedicated commitments + burst behavior: https://redwood.docs/internal/dedicated/prd-commit-burst-1
Maya P: core ask = define SLA targets by model-class + seq buckets, autoscale contract, billing for reserved vs burst, and acceptance tests. quick read pls.
Leo K: looking. we need explicit p50/p90/p99 by model family and short/med/long seqs. we can't promise flat p99. propose p99_short=250ms, p99_med=450ms, p99_long=800ms.
Shweta R: Acceptance criteria idea: can hold committed throughput for 72h with errors <1%; autoscale must restore capacity to handle +30% sustained within 90s; fallback to lower-cost compatible model should begin within 2s of saturation signal.
Dave SRE: ops checklist to include: health probes (liveness + kv-cache checksum), rolling deploy steps, tenant circuit-breaker rules, quota enforcement hooks. add regional failover playbook and runbook links.
Ana S: SE asks: add a \"burst reserve\" product knob: reserve X% of committed pool for short bursts (default 10m max). billing should show reserved vs burst usage separately. need sample invoice calc.
Maya P: good — I'll add billing example. also edge-case: multi-model pipelines (chain of calls). plan: sum tokens across calls and apply per-request multiplier; config key: `chain_token_multiplier`.
Leo K: sizing baseline for appendix: e.g., A100-like ~120 tokens/s for an 8k fp16 model at batch=1. publish a table: per_gpu_tokens_s by model-class and quantization. sample formula in doc: `required_gpus = ceil((peak_tokens_per_sec*safety_factor) / per_gpu_tokens_s)`
Dave SRE: proposed autoscale policy: min_replicas=2, scale_step=+25% up to 200%, cooldown=30s, scale_down_delay=10m. metric: custom tokens/s or sustained_gpu_util. never scale below committed_replicas unless tenant opts out.
Shweta R: add explicit gating in SLA: if customer has active commit, we won't scale below commit even if idle. acceptance tests must include a chair/test harness that simulates 72h at commit QPS. add regression test for p99 regressions measured by eval prompts.
Ana S: Sales: can we put fallback to Hosted in contract as an optional fallback? customers want explicit TOS text and potential SLA credit if fallback used. legal needs to weigh in.
Maya P: added rollout policy section: canary -> ramp -> full -> emergency fallback. emergency fallback requires Ops lead ack and immediate tenant notification. include webhook notify example.
ops-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5423 (maya)
Leo K: QA: include chaos scenarios: kill-gpu, network partition, cold-cache, noisy-tenant stampede. define expected behavior for each and instrumentation to capture p99/p90.
Dave SRE: include circuit-breaker thresholds and how they map to SLA credits. also document shunt-to-hosted flow and billing implications.
Maya P: action items: Leo -> sizing appendix & sample calc; Dave -> ops playbook + runbooks + playbook snippets; Ana -> billing language + TOS draft; Shweta -> acceptance test plan and harness spec. I'll fold changes and re-upload by EOD. :white_check_mark:
Leo K: one last note: publish a \"throughput per GPU\" table as CSV in appendix and a small python snippet for calc. e.g.``
# sample calc
import math
per_gpu=120
peak=14400  # tokens/s
safety=1.25
req=math.ceil((peak*safety)/per_gpu)
print(req)
``
Maya P: perfect. thanks everyone. will tag legal/sales where needed and loop back.
